# capi_machine_health_check (Resource)

A MachineHealthCheck of a cluster on the management cluster the provider block names: which machines are watched (one of `machine_deployment`, `control_plane` or `selector`), what makes one unhealthy, and when remediation is allowed. The object's API version follows the installed core provider; the v1beta2 and legacy spec shapes render from the same configuration. Import with `namespace/name`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Watch a node group's machines; replace one whose node is not Ready for 5m,
# as long as no more than 40% of the group is unhealthy at once.
resource "capi_machine_health_check" "workers" {
  cluster            = capi_cluster.prod.name
  namespace          = "capi"
  name               = "workers"
  machine_deployment = capi_machine_deployment.workers.name

  node_startup_timeout = "15m"
  unhealthy_node_conditions = [
    { type = "Ready", status = "Unknown", timeout = "5m" },
    { type = "Ready", status = "False", timeout = "5m" },
  ]

  remediation = { max_unhealthy = "40%" }
}

# Watch the control plane with the default checks; never remediate more than
# one machine at a time.
resource "capi_machine_health_check" "control_plane" {
  cluster       = capi_cluster.prod.name
  namespace     = "capi"
  name          = "control-plane"
  control_plane = true

  remediation = { max_unhealthy = "1" }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `cluster` (String) Name of the Cluster.
- `name` (String) Object name.

### Optional

- `control_plane` (Boolean) Watch the control-plane machines.
- `machine_deployment` (String) Watch the machines of this `capi_machine_deployment` (by its `name`), in either mode.
- `namespace` (String) Namespace of the Cluster. Default `default`.
- `node_startup_timeout` (String) How long a machine may go without a node before it is unhealthy, as a Go duration. CAPI's default is `10m`.
- `remediation` (Attributes) When and how unhealthy machines are remediated. Without it, the owner replaces each unhealthy machine while at most 100% are unhealthy. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--remediation))
- `selector` (Map of String) Watch the machines carrying these labels.
- `unhealthy_machine_conditions` (Attributes List) Machine conditions that make a machine unhealthy. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--unhealthy_machine_conditions))
- `unhealthy_node_conditions` (Attributes List) Node conditions that make a machine unhealthy. Default: `Ready` `Unknown` or `False` for `5m`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--unhealthy_node_conditions))
- `wait` (Attributes) What to wait for after the object is applied. Default conditions: RemediationAllowed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--wait))

### Read-Only

- `conditions` (Attributes List) The object's conditions. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions))
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `manifest` (String) The applied object as YAML.
- `status` (Attributes) The object's status. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--status))

<a id="nestedatt--remediation"></a>
### Nested Schema for `remediation`

Optional:

- `max_unhealthy` (String) Remediate only while at most this many machines are unhealthy: a count (`2`) or a percentage (`40%`). Exclusive with `unhealthy_range`.
- `template` (Attributes) An external remediation template (a Metal3 or custom remediation CRD) used instead of deleting the machine. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--remediation--template))
- `unhealthy_range` (String) Remediate only while the unhealthy count is in this range (`[1-3]`). Exclusive with `max_unhealthy`.

<a id="nestedatt--remediation--template"></a>
### Nested Schema for `remediation.template`

Required:

- `api_version` (String)
- `kind` (String)
- `name` (String)



<a id="nestedatt--unhealthy_machine_conditions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `unhealthy_machine_conditions`

Required:

- `status` (String) Condition status that is unhealthy (`False`, `Unknown`).
- `timeout` (String) How long the condition may hold before the machine is unhealthy, as a Go duration.
- `type` (String) Condition type (`Ready`).


<a id="nestedatt--unhealthy_node_conditions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `unhealthy_node_conditions`

Required:

- `status` (String) Condition status that is unhealthy (`False`, `Unknown`).
- `timeout` (String) How long the condition may hold before the machine is unhealthy, as a Go duration.
- `type` (String) Condition type (`Ready`).


<a id="nestedatt--wait"></a>
### Nested Schema for `wait`

Optional:

- `conditions` (List of String) Status conditions that must be `True`. An empty list waits for nothing.
- `timeout` (String) Go duration. Default `10m`.


<a id="nestedatt--conditions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `conditions`

Read-Only:

- `message` (String)
- `reason` (String)
- `status` (String)
- `type` (String)


<a id="nestedatt--status"></a>
### Nested Schema for `status`

Read-Only:

- `current_healthy` (Number)
- `expected_machines` (Number)
- `remediations_allowed` (Number)
- `targets` (List of String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
#!/bin/bash
# namespace/name of the MachineHealthCheck.
terraform import capi_machine_health_check.workers capi/workers
```
